title: Frustration and Conflict
summary: Frustration (blocking of goal-directed behaviour) and types of conflict: approach–approach, approach–avoidance, avoidance–avoidance, double approach–avoidance.
objectives: Define frustration and responses to it.
Describe the four types of conflict.
revision: Frustration (blocked goal-directed behaviour) and four conflict types: approach–approach, approach–avoidance, avoidance–avoidance, double approach–avoidance.
traps: Approach–approach = two desirable; avoidance–avoidance = two undesirable; approach–avoidance = one mixed goal.

notes.t: The emotional and behavioural response when goal-directed behaviour is blocked or thwarted.
Responses to frustration include aggression, regression, withdrawal, fixation and compromise.
Choosing between two desirable goals (e.g., two attractive job offers).
One goal has both attractive and unattractive aspects (e.g., a well-paid but stressful job).
Choosing between two undesirable options (e.g., two unpleasant tasks).
Two options, each with both positive and negative aspects.
UGC NET frequently asks to identify and distinguish the four conflict types.

mnemonics.title: AAAD
mnemonics.text: A — Approach–approach (two desirable), A — Approach–avoidance (mixed), A — Avoidance–avoidance (two undesirable), D — Double approach–avoidance (two mixed)

flashcards.a: Response when goal-directed behaviour is blocked.
One goal, mixed pros and cons.
